           PLAINTIFF,                                      FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT FOR:

   TRAVEL LLC, a limited liability company; and            2.    VIOLATION OF CALIFORNIA

                            FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT CLASS ACTION
      Case 3:25-cv-05075-AMO             Document 30        Filed 12/18/25      Page 2 of 10




 1                                            INTRODUCTION

 2          1.      Plaintiff LINDSEY CANNON (“Plaintiff”), by and through her counsel, brings this

 3 First Amended Complaint against Defendants ROBERT THEDE and ALL ROADS TRAVEL

 4 LLC to seek justice for thousands of students and travelers who were left stranded and defrauded.

 5 This case arises from a corporate shell game; a quintessential “heads I win, tails you lose”

 6 scenario. Defendant Thede and Andrew Citores co-founded JusTours. After selling the company

 7 for millions, Defendant Thede and Citores continued to operate it with reckless disregard for

 8 financial norms—soliciting funds from students while the company that bought JusTours was

 9 heading towards insolvency, periodically failing to pay employees, and relying on Citores’s

10 personal credit card and assumedly likewise relying on Thede’s personal credit card to pay for

11 JusTours customers’ travel services. When the scheme collapsed, Thede quickly abandoned this

12 sinking ship (and all of its massive liabilities for which it was woefully undercapitalized) and he

13 launched a “phoenix” entity, All Roads Travel. Then, literally within days, he and All Roads

14 Travel “licensed” the JusTours name and effectively continued as JusTours.

15                                     JURISDICTION AND VENUE

16          2.      Subject Matter Jurisdiction. This Court has original jurisdiction over this civil

17 action under the Class Action Fairness Act of 2005 (“CAFA”), 28 U.S.C. § 1332(d). The matter in

18 controversy exceeds the sum or value of $5,000,000, exclusive of interest and costs, and is a class

19 action in which: (a) there are 100 or more class members; and (b) at least one member of the class

20 of plaintiffs is a citizen of a State different from any defendant. Specifically, Plaintiff is a citizen

21 of California, and Defendant Robert Thede is a citizen of Nevada.

22          3.      Personal Jurisdiction. This Court has personal jurisdiction over Defendants

23 because they have purposefully availed themselves of the resources and protections of the State of

24 California. Defendants conducted substantial business in California, marketed and sold travel

25 services to California residents, and entered into contracts with residents of this District.

26          4.      Venue. Venue is proper in this District pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(2) because

27 a substantial part of the events or omissions giving rise to the claims occurred in this District,

28 including the solicitation of customers and the formation the contracts for travel services.

                                      FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT
                                                 1
      Case 3:25-cv-05075-AMO            Document 30        Filed 12/18/25      Page 3 of 10




 1

 2                                                 PARTIES

 3          5.      Plaintiff is an individual residing in Yolo County, California, and is a citizen of the

 4 State of California.

 5          6.      Defendant Robert Thede (“Thede”) is an individual believed to be residing in, and a

 6 citizen of, the State of Nevada.

 7                  a.      Thede as Seller of Travel Under California Law. Thede and Citores were

 8 co-founders and owners of JusTours, Inc. (dba “JusCollege”). Thede is also a founder, partner,

 9 officer, and the CRO of Defendant All Roads Travel LLC. After Thede and Citores sold JusTours,

10 they continued on as executives of the company that bought JusTours, including during the period

11 giving rise to this lawsuit. Citores used his personal credit card to pay for Plaintiff’s travel

12 services, and on information and belief, this was practice of both co-founders of JusTours such

13 that Thede likewise used his own personal credit card to pay for JusTours’s customers’ travel

14 services. On information and belief, Thede was also in control of JusTours during the period

15 giving rise to this lawsuit and in his individual capacity sold but left unfulfilled travel services

16 bought by Plaintiff and Class Members. Thede, like his co-founder Citores, is thus a “seller of

17 travel” pursuant to California Business & Professions Code § 17550.1.

18                  b.      The Alter Ego Scheme. A unity of interest and ownership exists between

19 Thede and JusTours such that any separateness between them ceased to exist. Plaintiff is informed

20 and believes that Thede, along with co-founder Citores, sold JusTours to Network Travel

21 Experiences/Pollen LLC for approximately $25 million in 2018. However, on information and

22 belief, the transaction included an "earn-out" provision whereby Thede continued to manage and

23 control the company’s operations as they had before the sale.

24                  c.      Reckless Disregard for Corporate Formalities. On information and

25 belief, during this earn-out period, Thede operated the company with a disregard for corporate

26 formalities and financial norms. On information and belief, Thede was so unfocused on corporate

27 distinctness that he allowed and/or directed his co-founder Citores (and assumedly himself) to pay

28 for travel services sold to customers using their own personal credit cards.

                                      FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT
                                                 2
      Case 3:25-cv-05075-AMO           Document 30        Filed 12/18/25      Page 4 of 10




 1                  d.     Insolvency and Labor Violations. Plaintiff is informed and believes that

 2 Thede continued to solicit sales from college students while knowing that JusTours was insolvent

 3 and unable to meet its financial obligations. In fact, on information and belief, Thede admitted in a

 4 podcast that employees were unpaid for more than two months—a clear violation of labor laws as

 5 well as an obvious signal of financial distress.

 6                  e.     Parent Company Recklessness. This pattern of illegality extended to

 7 JusTours’s parent entities, Network Travel Experiences and Pollen LLC. On information and

 8 belief, while failing to consistently pay employees, these entities spent lavishly on corporate

 9 parties and entertainment, prioritizing frivolous spending over basic legal obligations. Adherence

10 to the fiction of the separate existence of the corporation would, under these circumstances,

11 sanction a fraud and promote injustice.

12                  f.     Inequitable Result

13          An inequitable result will follow if Defendants are not held liable for the obligations of

14 JusTours. JusTours is defunct, insolvent, and unable to satisfy judgments, while Defendant Thede

15 and Defendant All Roads Travel retained the benefit of JusTours’s goodwill, customer

16 relationships, booking data, revenue streams, and on information and belief, credits from airlines,

17 hotels and others for travel services bought by JusTours for its customers but not provided to the

18 customers. Absent alter-ego liability, Plaintiff and the Classes will be left without any meaningful

19 remedy despite Defendants’ continuation of the same business operations and exploitation of the

20 same assets. Recognizing corporate separateness under these circumstances would sanction a

21 fraud, promote injustice, and permit Defendants to evade liability through corporate manipulation.

22          7.      Defendant All Roads Travel LLC. Defendant All Roads Travel LLC (“All Roads

23 Travel”) is a limited liability company that conducts business in California and is a “seller of

24 travel” pursuant to California Business & Professions Code § 17550.1.

25                  a.     Successor Liability / Mere Continuation. Plaintiff alleges that All Roads

26 Travel is the mere continuation and/or successor-in-interest to JusTours. This succession is

27 evidenced by: (i) a continuity of management by Defendant Thede and Citores; (ii) the use of the

28 same executives and employees; (iii) the acquisition of JusTours’s core assets, for inadequate or

                                     FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT
                                                3
      Case 3:25-cv-05075-AMO              Document 30        Filed 12/18/25     Page 5 of 10




 1 no consideration, specifically its customer lists and booking data, as well as, on information and

 2 belief, credits provided to JusTours by airlines, hotels, and others for travel services that were

 3 unutilized when JusTours failed to provide to travel services to its customers; (iv) All Roads

 4 Travel holding itself out to the public as the continuation of JusTours’s business; and (v) All

 5 Roads Travel expressly and impliedly assumed JusTours’s liabilities by providing the trips to

 6 JusTours customers that JusTours had sold but failed to provide and continuing JusTours’s

 7 contractual relationships while disclaiming responsibility for refund obligations.

 8           8.        Plaintiff is unaware of the true names of DOES 1 through 10. Plaintiff sues said

 9 defendants by said fictitious names and will amend this Complaint when the true names and

10 capacities are ascertained or when such facts pertaining to liability are ascertained, or as permitted

11 by law or by the Court. Plaintiff is informed and believes that each of the fictitiously named

12 defendants is in some manner responsible for the events and allegations set forth in this

13 Complaint.

14           9.        Plaintiff makes the allegations in this Complaint without any admission that, as to

15 any particular allegation, Plaintiff bears the burden of pleading, proving, or persuading and

16 Plaintiff reserves all of Plaintiff's right to plead in the alternative.

17                                        FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS

18           10.       The Business Model. Defendants operated a travel service business targeting

19 college students, selling air transportation, hotel accommodations and other travel services for

20 "Spring Break" and other excursions. Under California law, Defendants are "Sellers of Travel"

21 (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17550.1).

22           11.       Formation of the Contract. In approximately May 2019, Plaintiff contracted with

23 JusTours/JusCollege for a travel package to Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, scheduled for March/April

24 2020.

25                 o   The Confirmation: Plaintiff contacted Defendants via their digital platform/email,
                       purchased the specific travel services, dates and location, and received written
26
                       confirmation—via email and/or digital booking receipts—guaranteeing that the
27                     travel would be provided. On information and belief, this was the process by
                       which all contracts were formed between Defendants and Class Members.
28

                                        FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT
                                                   4
      Case 3:25-cv-05075-AMO             Document 30       Filed 12/18/25      Page 6 of 10




 1                o   Performance: Plaintiff paid the total cost of approximately $900.00 through a
                      series of payments thus meeting the only meaningful condition under the contract.
 2
                      On information and belief, Class Members similarly paid for travel and met
 3                    contractual conditions.

 4          12.       The Breach and Failure of Consideration. Defendants failed to provide the

 5 contracted air transportation and accommodations. When the travel was cancelled, Defendants did

 6 not refund the money as required by law and contract.

 7                o   Total Failure: For a substantial portion of the Class, including Plaintiff,
                      Defendants provided zero travel services and zero refunds, effectively retaining
 8
                      Class Members' funds while providing no consideration in return.
 9
                  o   The "Credit" Scheme: Instead of the refunds required by California law,
10                    Defendants offered worthless "credits," on information and belief, to ultimately be
                      serviced by the new entity, All Roads Travel.
11
            The contracts between Defendants and the Classes of its customers required Defendants to
12
     provide specific travel services on designated dates. In the event of cancellation or
13
     nonperformance, Defendants were obligated to refund all amounts paid. These obligations were
14
     memorialized in Defendants’ booking confirmations and payment receipts. Under these
15
     agreements, Defendants were required to either (a) provide the contracted air transportation and
16
     other travel services as promised or (b) promptly refund all monies paid for services not provided.
17
            13.       The Fraudulent Transfer. Following the financial collapse of the parent entity in
18
     the United Kingdom, on information and belief Defendant Thede engaged in a scheme to shed
19
     JusTours's refund liabilities while retaining its profitable assets. On information and belief, Thede
20
     formed or utilized All Roads Travel to acquire the customer database and booking records of
21
     JusTours and the credits provided to JusTours by airlines, hotels, and others for travel services that
22
     were unutilized when JusTours failed to provide to travel services to its customers. On information
23
     and belief, All Roads Travel paid little to no consideration for these assets under the guise of a
24
     $5,000 “license fee,” to evade creditors, avoid refunding the students, and to obtain credits for
25
     travel services provided to JusTours by airlines, hotels and others.
26
     ///
27
     ///
28

                                       FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT
                                                  5
      Case 3:25-cv-05075-AMO             Document 30       Filed 12/18/25      Page 7 of 10




 1                                   CLASS ACTION ALLEGATIONS

 2          14.       Class Definitions. Plaintiff brings this action pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil

 3 Procedure 23 on behalf of:

 4                o   The California Class: All individuals who, while in California, purchased travel
                      services that Defendants sold or arranged, but to whom said services were not
 5
                      provided and to whom the money was not refunded.
 6
                  o   The Nationwide Class: All individuals who, while in the United States, purchased
 7                    travel services that Defendants sold or arranged, but to whom said services were
                      not provided and to whom the money was not refunded.
 8
            15.       Rule 23 Requirements.
 9
                      a. Numerosity: The Class consists of thousands of students, making joinder
10
                         impracticable.
11
                      b. Commonality & Predominance: Common questions predominate, including:
12                       whether Defendants are the alter ego of the corporate entities; whether All
                         Roads Travel is a successor-in-interest; whether Defendants breached contracts
13
                         with customers and failed to provide refunds; and whether Defendants violated
14                       California’s Seller of Travel statutes.

15                    c. Typicality: Plaintiff’s claims are identical to those of the Class—she paid for a
                         trip she never received and was denied a refund.
16
                      d. Adequacy: Plaintiff has no conflicts of interest and has retained experienced
17
                         class counsel.
18
                      e. Superiority: A class action is the only efficient method for adjudicating these
19                       claims given the relatively small size of individual damages compared to the
                         cost of litigation.
20
                                            CAUSES OF ACTION
21
                                       FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION
22                        Violation of California Unfair Competition Law (UCL)
                                 (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 17200, et seq.)
23                       (Against All Defendants on Behalf of the California Class)
24
            16.       Defendants committed acts of unfair competition by engaging in unlawful, unfair,
25
     and fraudulent business practices. Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17200.
26
            17.       Unlawful: Defendants violated the California Sellers of Travel Law (Cal. Bus. &
27
     Prof. Code §§ 17550 et seq.) by failing to make required disclosures and failing to issue refunds
28
     for unprovided travel services when required under California law.

                                       FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT
                                                  6
      Case 3:25-cv-05075-AMO             Document 30        Filed 12/18/25      Page 8 of 10




 1           18.     Unfair: Defendants’ conduct—soliciting funds while insolvent, spending lavishly

 2 on parties while stiffing employees, and transferring assets to a new entity to avoid debt—is

 3 immoral, unethical, and substantially injurious to consumers.

 4           19.     Plaintiff seeks restitution, disgorgement of all unlawfully-withheld gains, and a

 5 public injunction.

 6                                    SECOND CAUSE OF ACTION
                               Violation of California Sellers of Travel Law
 7                               (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 17550, et seq.)
                         (Against All Defendants on Behalf of the California Class)
 8
             20.     Under California Business & Professions Code § 17550.14, a seller of travel must
 9
     refund all moneys paid for travel services not actually provided by the earlier of thirty days of the
10
     scheduled departure or cancellation or three days from the day the seller of travel is first unable to
11
     provide the travel services.
12
             21.     Defendants failed to provide the travel services bought by Plaintiff and members of
13
     the California Class and failed to remit the refunds within the statutory period.
14
             22.     As sellers of travel in their own right and as the alter ego and/or successor-in-
15
     interest to the selling entity, Defendants Thede and All Roads Travel are personally and jointly
16
     liable for these statutory violations.
17
                                    THIRD CAUSE OF ACTION
18                                        Breach of Contract
              (Against All Defendants on Behalf of the California and Nationwide Classes)
19

20           23.     Plaintiff and Class Members entered into valid, binding contracts with Defendants,

21 evidenced by email confirmations and digital receipts.

22           24.     Plaintiff and Class Members performed by paying for the travel services in full.

23           25.     Defendants breached these contracts by failing to provide the agreed-upon travel

24 services and by failing to refund Plaintiff’s and Class Members’ payments following cancellation

25 and nonperformance, despite their full performance and compliance with all contractual

26 obligations.

27 ///

28 ///

                                       FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT
                                                  7
      Case 3:25-cv-05075-AMO            Document 30        Filed 12/18/25         Page 9 of 10




 1          26.     Successor Liability: Defendant All Roads Travel is liable for this breach as the

 2 mere continuation of JusTours. All Roads Travel fraudulently acquired the assets of JusTours to

 3 avoid creditors and stands in the shoes of the original contracting party.

 4          27.     Plaintiff and the Class have suffered damages in the amount of the payments made

 5 to Defendants.

 6                                        PRAYER FOR RELIEF

 7 WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays for judgment as follows:

 8          1.      Certifying the California and Nationwide Classes and appointing Plaintiff as Class

 9                  Representative and her counsel as Class Counsel;

10          2.      Declaring that All Roads Travel LLC is the successor-in-interest to JusTours, Inc.;

11          3.      Declaring that Robert Thede is the alter ego of JusTours, Inc.;

12          4.      Awarding restitution, disgorgement, refunds, and equitable relief under the UCL
                    and the Seller of Travel statutes in the amount of $20,000,000.00;
13
            5.      Awarding compensatory damages for breach of contract in the amount of
14
                    $25,000,000.00;
15
            6.      Issuing a Public Injunction enjoining Defendants from committing future violations
16                  of California’s Sellers of Travel Law;

17          7.      Awarding attorneys’ fees and costs pursuant to Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 1021.5 and
                    other applicable laws; and
18
            8.      Granting such other relief as the Court deems just.
19

20                                    DEMAND FOR JURY TRIAL

21          Plaintiff hereby demands a trial by jury on all issues so triable.

22
